audit_notes: Model: steady 1D series conduction interior -> wall -> nanowood panel with sol-air Robin boundary; q = [alpha*I + h*dT - eps*R_net]/(1 + h*R_tot). Adjustments: the proposal's aged SR 0.75 and k 0.03 are dry, fresh laboratory values. Delignified cellulose outdoors photo-yellows (UV oxidation of cellulose forms chromophores even without lignin), greys by mould and soils; a 20-year life-mean SR of ~0.65 is more realistic even with a hydrophobic siloxane treatment. Moisture uptake (cellulose equilibrium moisture 5-10 %) raises the transverse conductivity to ~0.04 W/mK. Hand result with the audited values: R_panel = 0.02/0.04 = 0.5 m2K/W, q = (0.35*180 + 150 - 0.93*40)/(1 + 15*2.5) = 175.8/38.5 = 4.57 W/m2 vs 5.59 W/m2 for aged white paint directly on the wall: -18 %, almost all from the added resistance. Structural: nanowood has high longitudinal strength (~100 MPa after densification; non-densified nanowood ~10-20 MPa), fine for cladding, but wet/dry cycling causes swelling and cracking; combustible. Durability for 20 years outdoors is the decisive weakness. Simulation coefficient: effective conductance 1/(R_tot + 1/h) = 0.39 W/m2K.
